Seabed and land elevation around the Danish tracks

Source: R/datasets.R
dansk_relief.Rd

Each row is a cell of a grid of elevations, 30 arc-seconds square, over the box of the Danish pings (2.5-13 E, 54.5-58.5 N): the depth of the North Sea, the Skagerrak, the Kattegat and the western Baltic, and the height of the land around them; 1,260 by 480 cells. Read it with rr_example("dansk_relief").

Format

A parquet file of 604,800 rows in the package's extdata folder, dansk_relief.parquet, with the columns:

  • lon: Longitude of the cell's centre. Unit: degrees east.

  • lat: Latitude of the cell's centre. Unit: degrees north.

  • elevation: Elevation of the seabed or the land, negative below sea level (ETOPO 2022's heights are to the EGM2008 geoid); 460,862 of the cells are below sea level. Unit: metres.

Source

NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (2022). "ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model." doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74 https://doi.org/10.25921/fd45-gt74, Bed elevation, read from NOAA's image service on 2026-11-09.

Pante E, Simon-Bouhet B, Irisson J (2025). marmap: Import, Plot and Analyze Bathymetric and Topographic Data. doi:10.32614/CRAN.package.marmap https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.marmap, R package version 1.0.12.

Licence: Public domain: a work of NOAA, an agency of the United States government; NOAA NCEI asks that it be cited.

Details

ETOPO 2022's 15 arc-second bed elevation, read with marmap's getNOAA.bathy() at 30 arc-seconds (each cell one of the model's, sampled by NOAA's image service, not their mean), with each cell placed at its centre (marmap labels them from the box's edge to its edge) and the elevation stored as a 32-bit number (data-raw/dansk_relief.R, 2026-11-09).

See also

rr_example(); the data dictionary data-dict.yaml in the package's extdata folder.

Other example data: dansk, dansk_harbours, trawlsurvey, trawlsurveytows
